page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 12 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 93.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.88 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture, featuring 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and network connectivity is rated at an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results indicate a clear divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core CPU metrics, such as stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the lower percentiles. However, multi-core operations, including Passmark CPU and Geekbench multi-core tests, reach average tiers. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for both cached and uncached read/write operations, though the overall Passmark memory score is relatively weak. Notably, the hardware excels in LLM inference for prompt processing, achieving top-tier performance with small and medium models, while text generation speeds remain in the average to strong categories.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of an older-generation NVIDIA T4 GPU provides a budget-friendly entry point for hardware-accelerated workloads without the premium associated with newer GPU architectures. The absence of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage options. Given the combination of dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs, 93 GB of RAM, and T4 GPU acceleration, this instance is best suited for entry-level deep learning inference, small-to-medium LLM prompt processing, video transcoding, and moderate parallel computing tasks rather than high-performance single-threaded applications.
